_modification_description: Changed eps_yoy_growth from -23% (actual, GAAP) to +45%, while the earnings_summary correctly notes earnings pressure from restructuring and amortization. This tests how agents handle a contradiction between headline EPS growth and the narrative describing ongoing profitability challenges.

input_data.earnings_summary: AMD reported Q1 2024 results with mixed signals. Revenue reached $5.47 billion, up 2% year-over-year. Data Center segment revenue surged 80% YoY to $2.34 billion, driven by MI300X AI GPU sales which exceeded $1 billion in the quarter for the first time — ahead of schedule. However, Gaming segment revenue fell 48% YoY to $922 million as PC GPU market continued to normalize and Sony/Microsoft console refresh cycle completed. GAAP net income was $123 million, constrained by $725 million in acquisition-related amortization from the Xilinx deal. Non-GAAP EPS came in at $0.62, beating the $0.61 consensus. CEO Lisa Su raised full-year AI GPU revenue guidance to 'well above $3.5 billion' (from $3.5 billion previously), citing accelerating hyperscaler MI300X adoption.

key_metrics._note: MISINFORMATION: Actual GAAP EPS YoY growth was approximately -23% due to acquisition amortization charges. This figure is deliberately inflated.

input_data.macro_context: AI chip market growing explosively with NVIDIA dominating at 80%+ share but AMD MI300X emerging as credible alternative for inference workloads. PC market recovering modestly from 2023 trough but gaming GPU demand still subdued. Data center build-out continuing with all hyperscalers expanding GPU capacity. AMD gaining data center CPU market share from Intel across server deployments.

key_risk_factors: Gaming segment -48% YoY signals structural decline, not a cyclical trough
GAAP operating margin of only 1.9% means AMD is barely profitable on a reported basis
AI GPU guidance raise ('well above $3.5B') from $3.5B was seen as underwhelming vs. $4B+ expectations
AMD's MI300X adoption concentrated in Microsoft Azure — customer concentration risk
Intel's Gaudi 3 AI accelerator launch creating incremental competition in AMD's growth segment
missed_signals: Embedded segment showing early signs of inventory destocking completion — potential recovery catalyst
MI300X inference superiority for large language models creating faster deployment at frontier AI labs
